name: Violaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use stipules, a 5-merous often zygomorphic flower, five close-set stamens with enlarged anther connectives, a superior 1-locular parietal ovary and a 3-valved capsule.

project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas Viola + Pombalia family module
project_scope.note: Viola is visually obvious; Pombalia is the important anti-stereotype showing that not every violet-family plant looks like a classic violet.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Check for stipules, then inspect a 5-part flower: 5 free petals, often unequal, 5 stamens closely surrounding the ovary with prominent connective appendages, and a superior 1-locular ovary with parietal placentation.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Herbs to shrubs globally; project taxa are herbs/perennial geophytes. Leaves are simple, usually alternate, and stipules are present.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually bisexual and 5-merous, often zygomorphic. In Viola the lower/anterior petal is strongly spurred; Pombalia may be less stereotypically violet-like but retains the family reproductive architecture.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Usually a 3-valved loculicidal capsule; seeds often bear an elaiosome.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Stipules + 5 close-set stamens/anther scales + one-celled parietal ovary + 3-valved capsule is safer than 'purple flower with a spur.'

visual_lesson.teaching_order: stipule → 5-part zygomorphic flower → anther-connective scale/pollen cone → 1-locular parietal ovary → 3-valved capsule → Viola-vs-Pombalia
visual_lesson.intro: Classic violets are easy, but the family lesson matters because Pombalia can look nothing like the garden-violet stereotype.

steps.title: 1 · Find the stipules
steps.look_for: A pair of stipules at the leaf base; in Viola they may be obvious and leafy or finely divided.
steps.why_it_matters: A reliable vegetative clue before the flower is studied.

steps.title: 2 · Read the asymmetric 5-petal flower
steps.look_for: Five free petals, often unequal; in Viola the lowermost/anterior petal carries a backward spur.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the classic family gestalt but not the whole diagnosis.

steps.title: 3 · Look at the anthers, not just the petals
steps.look_for: Five stamens close around the ovary; the anther connectives extend into noticeable scales/appendages. In strongly zygomorphic flowers the lower stamens can bear nectary appendages into the spur.
steps.why_it_matters: This structure ties Viola and less obvious Violaceae together.

steps.title: 4 · Confirm the one-chamber ovary and 3-valved capsule
steps.look_for: Superior 1-locular ovary with parietal placentas, later splitting into three broad valves.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates Violaceae from the 3-locular columella capsules of Euphorbiaceae.

steps.title: 5 · Pombalia is the anti-stereotype
steps.look_for: A small non-classic violet-family herb/geophyte retaining the stipules, 5-merous flower and capsular family architecture.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents overfitting the family to Viola alone.

comparisons.title: Violaceae vs Euphorbiaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can end in a 3-valved capsule, but Violaceae has a 1-locular ovary with parietal placentation; Euphorbiaceae typically has 3 locules, one ovule each and a persistent central columella.

comparisons.title: Violaceae vs Salicaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have a 1-locular parietal ovary, but local Salicaceae uses reduced unisexual catkin flowers and many comose seeds; Violaceae uses 5-merous bisexual flowers and usually a 3-valved capsule.

comparisons.title: Violaceae vs Polygalaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can look strongly zygomorphic. Violaceae is stipulate and has five close-set stamens with distinctive connective appendages; Polygalaceae lacks stipules and has a very different keel/wing flower architecture.

visual_lesson.caveat: Not all Violaceae are spurred or strongly zygomorphic. The ovary/placentation + stamen-connective structure is the broader family anchor.

genera.fast_cue: stipulate herb + strongly zygomorphic flower + spurred lower petal + 3-valved capsule
less stereotypical violet-family herb; use stipules, 5-merous flower and capsule anatomy

taxonomy_notes: Pombalia verticillata is accepted under current Kew; older sources may use Hybanthus verticillatus.

visual_targets.annotation_goal: connect lower petal spur to staminal nectary appendage
show parietal placentas on opened valves
teach family without classic Viola gestalt
